subject: E4.1 step 3 DONE s358i (2d9aa8b): v1's file-level transpile surface deleted — parse_file/parse_code + lenient_ppi/_ppi_with_fallback gone; parse() survives as the prototype-collection walker ONLY (guarded die otherwise; the extractors are its sole callers). E4.1 COMPLETE.
description:
MEASURED s356 (at 1e891d0, after the #242 flip). The plan's step-3 premise is VOID and the deletion must not proceed as written.

Plan §5 step 3 says: delete `parse()` entry, `_assemble_output`, `_insert_variable_forward_declarations`, `parse_file`/`parse_code`, lenient-ppi path (~550 lines), and: "Verify each is truly unreachable (grep + gate) before deleting."

THE VERIFICATION SAYS DO NOT DELETE. Guardrail §5a.6's proof (a) — zero grep callers — FAILS:

**27 of the 131 gate files call Pl::Parser's file-level entry directly** (`Pl::Parser->new(code=>…)->parse()` or `Pl::Parser->parse_code(…)`):
  argv-01 autoviv-01 bless-01 constants-01 decl-ordering-01 default-underscore-01
  deref-args-01 errno-01 eval-01 file-line-01 goto-label-01 inheritance-01
  local-elem-01 local-elem-02 local-glob-01 local-symref-01 loop-body-context-01
  loop-labels-01 magic-vars-01 our-local-01 parser-01 prototype-01 signatures-01
  statements-01 string-funcs-01 use-require-01 utf8-source-01

That is ~664 assertion rows, and the MAJORITY are SHAPE assertions on v1's emitted CL text (`like($cl, qr/…/)`) — e.g. inheritance-01 83/86, deref-args-01 28/28, our-local-01 27/27, string-funcs-01 20/20. They pin v1's output FORMAT, so they cannot simply be re-pointed at Parser2: v2 emits differently, and each regex would need rewriting against a decision about what v2's shape should be.

`_assemble_output` and `_insert_variable_forward_declarations` are called from inside `parse()` (Parser.pm:866-868), so they are live for exactly the same reason. Effectively NOTHING in the ~550-line list is deletable while these 27 files exist.

THE ONE GENUINELY DEAD PIECE (not shipped — §5a.6 wants all step-3 deletions in ONE commit, so it waits for the re-scope): v1's `lenient_ppi` attribute (Parser.pm:129, used 786/793) and `_ppi_with_fallback` (Parser.pm:802+, "Only called when lenient_ppi is set"). pl2cl now DELETES the lenient_ppi opt and never hands it to a parser, and none of the 27 test files set it. The runners still pass `--lenient-ppi` on the command line (run-perl-test.pl, run-perl-suite.pl:410, sweep-perl-tests.pl:128, run-dist-t.pl:58) but it is inert by design (#242).

THE ASK — three options, materially different cost, and one deletes tests (CLAUDE.md requires user sign-off for that):
 (a) PORT the 27 files to Parser2. Honest but large: most assertions are v1-shape regexes that need rewriting, and the rewrite is only meaningful once someone decides the intended v2 shape per case. Risks silently weakening coverage while "passing".
 (b) RETIRE them. Defensible: they are shape tests for a pipeline no user can now reach, and the v2 suite (transpile-test-*.t) tests BEHAVIOUR against the perl oracle, which is strictly stronger. But 664 rows is a lot to drop on a "likely duplicated" argument — it needs a per-file coverage check, and it is the user's call.
 (c) KEEP v1's file entry as an explicitly-labelled TEST-ONLY API, documented as such; step 3 shrinks to the lenient-ppi deletion, and the ~550 lines go later, retired naturally as E5 burns down v1's statement layer (which those tests exercise anyway).

RECOMMENDATION: (c) now + (b)-per-file as E5 proceeds. It keeps one revert-able story, does not delete 664 rows on an unverified assumption, and matches the review's own re-scoping (docs/v2-code-review.md §4: "restate E4.1/E5 as a burn-down, not a deletion" — the 22k→14k arrives via E5 steps, not here).

NOTE: #244 (step 4 full verification) does NOT depend on this — it can run against the shipped flip.
